cohort: 20,092 infants of 22 to 27 weeks' gestation with a birth weight of 401 to 1500 g born at centers participating in the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Neonatal Research Network from 2002 to 2016
finding: While improvements in adjusted rates of mortality and most major morbidities did not differ by race/ethnicity among extremely preterm infants, rates of neurodevelopmental impairment increased in all groups.
mod_finding: Rates of cesarean delivery were initially lower among black and Hispanic infants compared with white infants, but these differences decreased over time.
